purpose: Review the historical Guinayangan marine sanctuary and reef name trail and the former municipal fishery page as CALABARZON source-discovery context. This is not a fish survey, legal-status verification, boundary study, or complete Ragay Gulf checklist.
searchMethod: Bounded public-web discovery on 2026-11-01 using exact sanctuary/reef names with Guinayangan, fish, species, survey, boundary, and sanctuary terms; directly reviewed the former municipal ordinance index, tourism page, fishery page, PSA barangay listing, and CRMP 2004 directory text. This is not an exhaustive agency, legal, or scientific-literature search.
searchQueries: site:denr.gov.ph Guinayangan Nabangka fish sanctuary fish survey
site:repository.nfrdi.da.gov.ph Guinayangan Ragay Gulf fish species

sourcesReviewed.citation: Coastal Resource Management Project. 2004. Directory of CRM Learning Destinations in the Philippines. CRMP Document No. 03-CRM/2004.
sourcesReviewed.reviewedLocation: Printed pages 2 and 69; PDF pages 3 and 78
sourcesReviewed.result: The directory says destination entries were submitted by about 80 LGUs and describes itself as a quick guide. The Guinayangan entry names Nabangka fish sanctuary at Barangay Capuluan Central and Capuluan reef (also known as Palad reef). The title page permits reproduction or quotation with proper reference.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Historical named-place and barangay context only; no coordinates, sanctuary boundary, fish taxa, fish survey, field dates, or current legal status.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Municipality of Guinayangan, former municipal website. Existing Ordinances index, Ordinance No. 7-2000.
sourcesReviewed.result: The legacy index lists Ordinance No. 7-2000, titled an ordinance establishing a fish sanctuary in Guinayangan, says it is also known as the Nabangka Fish Sanctuary, and gives an approval date of 15 December 2000. No ordinance text, map, or technical schedule was retrieved.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Historical ordinance-index lead only; not proof of the actual instrument, current legal validity, fishing restrictions, boundary geometry, or fish presence.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Municipality of Guinayangan, legacy tourism page. Natures Wonder / Palad Reef.
sourcesReviewed.result: The page places Palad Reef in Barangay Capuluan Central, describes coral and aquarium fishes in general terms, and calls it proposed to serve as another municipal fish sanctuary. It is legacy and carries a 2002 site copyright footer.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Historical reef locality context only. Generic aquarium-fish wording is not a taxa list or fish survey; 'proposed' is not evidence of declaration.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Municipality of Guinayangan, former municipal website. Marine Products / Fishery.
sourcesReviewed.result: Introduces its list as some fish catch in the municipal waters of Guinayangan (Ragay Gulf), then prints 13 vernacular labels: Alumahan, Tangige, Tulingan, Sapatero, Bisugo, Bangus, Kanoping, Malakapas, Sapsap, Tunsoy, Samaral, Dalagang Bukid, and Banak. No date is given for the catch list; the footer says copyright 2002.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Old municipality-wide catch-name discovery list only. Do not resolve labels to scientific taxa or assign them to Nabangka, Palad Reef, a station, date, gear, or current occurrence.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Philippine Statistics Authority. Guinayangan, Quezon PSGC barangay listing as of 31 July 2025.
sourcesReviewed.result: PSA lists Capuluan Central as Guinayangan barangay code 0405618011.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Administrative name/code cross-check only; not a marine boundary or fish evidence.

siteCrosswalk.outcome: Historical directory and legacy ordinance index independently name Nabangka; the directory locates it in Capuluan Central. No boundary, current status, or site-specific fish survey was retrieved.
The 2004 directory equates Capuluan Reef and Palad Reef; the legacy tourism page locates Palad in Capuluan Central and says it was proposed for another sanctuary. Keep it separate from Nabangka.
The legacy municipal fishery page is a broad catch-label lead only; its 13 vernacular labels are not scientific taxa or records from either named reef/sanctuary.

vernacularCatchLabels.taxonomyCrosswalkOutcome: Not attempted; names remain source-spelled vernacular labels because the page supplies no identification key, catch record, scientific names, or taxon-to-capture crosswalk.

geometryAndLegalStatus.note: Sources provide names and barangay context, not a georeferenced footprint or legal technical description. The legacy ordinance index is not the instrument.

limitations: The 2004 CRMP directory is a historical CRM-learning guide based on submitted LGU entries, not a fish survey or legal cadastre.
The municipal pages are legacy pages with a 2002 copyright footer; content publication date, methods, and current status are not established.
The ordinance index supplies a title, alias, and approval date but not ordinance text, technical boundary, amendments, repeal history, or present enforceability.
Palad Reef's legacy municipal description says it was proposed as another fish sanctuary; do not conflate it with the separately named Nabangka Fish Sanctuary.
The 13 Ragay Gulf labels are vernacular catch-list entries without species identities, field dates, stations, gear, catch records, vouchers, or a usable currentness basis.
No coordinates, geometry, taxon assertions, current occurrence, abundance, diet, catchability, safety, legal fishing advice, or app rows are established.
nextAction: Seek a retrievable copy of Ordinance No. 7-2000 and any approved technical boundary/map for Nabangka, then prioritize dated, station-resolved, rights-cleared fish surveys for Nabangka or Palad Reef. Keep the historical Gulf catch labels as unresolved vernacular discovery leads.
